title: Straighten a stack of three cartons whose middle carton has slid out from under the top one
instruction: The blue middle carton in this stack has slid out of line. Straighten the stack so all three cartons sit squarely on top of each other, without tipping the white top carton, which holds glass vials.
context: Stockers and order fillers (about 2.8 million US workers) straighten stock that has shifted in a stack as routine shelf and storeroom work. A middle carton that slides out leaves the one above half supported: pulling it back with the load still on top tips the load off, so the top carton is held or set aside first, the layer is put back, and the stack is rebuilt square.
setup: Distances are measured forward from the line through the two arm bases and left or right of the midline between them. Three loose cartons, each 14 x 5 x 4 cm (long x wide x tall), 0.30 kg, cardboard: brown (bottom), blue (middle), white (top, holding glass vials). They are stacked on the table on the midline, long edges pointing straight away from the arms. The brown carton's centre is 24 cm forward (its near end at 17 cm, far end at 31 cm). The white carton is directly above the brown one, edges in line. The blue carton between them is in line sideways but 5 cm farther from the arms (near end at 22 cm, far end at 36 cm), so 5 cm of it sticks out past the far end of the stack and the nearest 5 cm of the white carton has nothing under it. The stack stands still like this; nothing is falling at the start. Three distractors lie behind the stack, loose, and are not part of the task: a red ceramic mug (11.4 x 9 x 8 cm with handle, 0.30 kg) centred 48 cm forward and 24 cm left; a roll of clear tape (10 cm across, 5 cm high, 0.06 kg) lying flat, centred 49 cm forward and 24 cm right; and a Phillips screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 3.4 cm handle, 0.10 kg) lying left to right on the midline, 48 cm forward. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: 0 if the white top carton's top face is tilted more than 20 degrees from level at any moment of the trial, whatever happens afterwards. Otherwise the last moment of the trial is judged. A stack counts only if all three cartons are still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) and level (under 3 degrees of tilt), the brown carton is on the table, the blue carton lies on the brown one and the white carton lies on the blue one. For a stack, three numbers are measured from above: the larger of the two centre-to-centre horizontal offsets (blue to brown, white to blue), the larger of the two angles between the long edges of a carton and the one below it, and how far the brown carton's centre is from where it started. 1.0 if these are at most 1.5 cm, 10 degrees and 2 cm (the trial ends early once this has held for 3 seconds); 0.5 if not, but they are at most 3 cm, 20 degrees and 5 cm; 0 beyond that. Anything that is not such a stack scores 0: the stack left as it was (its offsets are 5 cm), a carton on the table or held in the air, the wrong order. Taking the white carton off and setting it on the table while the blue one is put back is allowed, as is holding it in a gripper meanwhile. The distractors are not scored.
reset_notes: Stack brown, then blue 5 cm toward the far side, then white directly above brown; put back any distractor that moved. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena (PhysX at 240 Hz, 20 Hz control) on a replica of a calibrated YAM station. The cartons are rigid boxes the size of small boxes of vials (14 x 5 x 4 cm; the arms' reach limits the stack to 12 cm) that do not crush or deform. The mug, tape and screwdriver are NVIDIA SimReady props. All surfaces have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), above cardboard's, so a carton pushed with a load on it drags the stack rather than sliding under it. No force sensing.
